## 2. Import CVFS data: Labour Outmigration, Agricultural Productivity and Food Security, Nepal, 2064-2072
```{r}
# A. Load data
github_remittance_url <- paste0(
  "https://github.com/ellenthickman/687Project/raw/",
  "refs/heads/main/36755-0001-Data.rda"
)

temp_env <- new.env()
loaded_names <- load(url(github_remittance_url), envir = temp_env)

loaded_names
remit_w <- temp_env[[loaded_names[1]]]

# B. Select variables
tv_prefixes <- c(
  "A10_", "B11C_", "B12C_", "B13C_",
  "B14C_", "B15C_", "B16B_", "B17_1B_", "B17_2B_",
  "B17_3B_", "B17_4B_", "B17_5B_", "B17_6B_",
  "B17_7B_", "C18_", "C19_", "C20_", "D30B_", "D31B_", "C21_", "REM"
)

remit_w <- remit_w |>
  select(
    HHID,
    ETHNICITY,
    starts_with(tv_prefixes),
    -ends_with(c("63", "72")) # Excluding year 2063 due to missing data in gfp indicator and 2072 due to missing variables and missing conversion data
  ) 

# C. Transform from wide to long
remit_l <- remit_w |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches(
      paste0(
        "^(",
        paste(tv_prefixes, collapse = "|"),
        ")(64|65|66|67|68|69|70|71)$" 
      )
    ),
    names_to = c(".value", "year"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*?)(64|65|66|67|68|69|70|71)$",
    names_transform = list(year = as.integer)
  )
```
## 3. Clean Data
```{r}
# A. Create a gross farm product
## i. Convert KG amounts to rupees per kg using Ministry of Agriculture data: https://caidmp.gov.np/downloadsfiles/special-issue-book-2072_price-%281%29-1692180081.pdf 
### Download data
library(readxl)

conversion_url <- "https://github.com/ellenthickman/687Project/raw/refs/heads/main/conversion.xlsx"

tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
download.file(conversion_url, tmp, mode = "wb")

conversion_data <- read_excel(tmp)

unlink(tmp)

### Lowercase all column names
conversion_data <- conversion_data %>% rename_with(tolower)

### Convert long data to wide format
conversion_w <- conversion_data %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = commodities,  # Column containing the future header names
    values_from = rupees_per_kg,  # Column containing the actual data values
    names_prefix = "price_"      # This creates columns like price_B11C_ so names don't clash
  )

### Join by year and multiply each crop column by its matching price column
remit_l <- remit_l %>%
  left_join(conversion_w, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(
    # Multiply the KG amounts by the matching rupee per kg prices
    B11C_rupees = B11C_ * price_B11C_,
    B12C_rupees = B12C_ * price_B12C_,
    B13C_rupees = B13C_ * price_B13C_,
    B14C_rupees = B14C_ * price_B14C_,
    B15C_rupees = B15C_ * price_B15C_
  ) %>%
  # Optional: drop the temporary price columns to keep your dataset clean
  select(-starts_with("price_"))

## ii. Set variable list
gfp_vars <- c("B11C_rupees", # Rice (KG originally)
              "B12C_rupees", # Maize (KG originally)
              "B13C_rupees", # Wheat (KG originally)
              "B14C_rupees", # Mustard (KG originally)
              "B15C_rupees", # Red Lentil (KG originally)
              "B16B_", # Vegetable
              "B17_1B_", # Buckwheat
              "B17_2B_", # Finger millet
              "B17_3B_", # Sesame
              "B17_4B_", # Kidney bean
              "B17_5B_", # Pea/gram
              "B17_6B_", # Cowpea/bean
              "B17_7B_", # Other crops
              "D30B_", # Poultry production
              "D31B_") # Other farming production

## iii. Mutate to generate gfp indicator
remit_l <- remit_l |>
  mutate(
    across(
      any_of(gfp_vars),
      ~ as.numeric(as.character(.x))
    ),
    gfp = rowSums(across(any_of(gfp_vars)), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

## iv. Drop extraneous variables 
remit_l <- remit_l |>
  select(-any_of(gfp_vars))
```

```{r}
# B. Rename variables
remit_l <- remit_l |>
  rename(
    rem = REM,
    hired_lab = C21_,
    land_owned = A10_,
    hhid = HHID,
    ethnic = ETHNICITY,
    tractor_time = C18_,
    thresher_used = C19_,
    motor_used = C20_
  )
```

```{r}
# C. Create farm technology indicator
remit_l <- remit_l |>
  mutate(
    tractor_used = case_when(
      tractor_time == 0 ~ 0,
      tractor_time > 0 & tractor_time <= 6600 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    across(c(thresher_used, motor_used),
           ~ case_when(
             as.character(.x) %in% c("(0) No" , "0")  ~ 0,
             as.character(.x) %in% c("(1) Yes", "1")  ~ 1,
             TRUE ~ NA_real_)),
    farm_tech = tractor_used + thresher_used + motor_used)
```

```{r}
# D. Transform land owned from a time variant to a time invariant variable
# i. Summary of land owned by year
remit_l |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    Min = min(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1 = quantile(land_owned, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean = mean(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3 = quantile(land_owned, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max = max(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  kable(caption = "Summary of land owned by year (Katha)")

## ii. View who has changed in land ownership over the years
remit_l |>
  group_by(hhid) |>
  summarize(distinct_values = n_distinct(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  count(distinct_values)

tv_land <- remit_l |>
  group_by(hhid) |>
  filter(n_distinct(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) |>
  ungroup(); tv_land

land_variance <- remit_l |>
  group_by(hhid) |>
  filter(n_distinct(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) |> # Optional: keep to only look at varying households
  summarize(
    land_var = var(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ); land_variance

## iii. Create an average
remit_l <- remit_l |>
    group_by(hhid) |>
  mutate(
    land_avg = mean(land_owned, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```
We have 571 (25%) of households whose landownership changes across the 9 years. Does it change drastically? Do we take the starting value, end value, or average?

### G. Check missing values vs 0 sales
```{r}
raw_data <- temp_env[[loaded_names[1]]]

check_vars <- c(
  "B11C_", "B12C_", "B13C_", "B14C_", "B15C_",
  "B16B_",
  "B17_1B_", "B17_2B_", "B17_3B_", "B17_4B_",
  "B17_5B_", "B17_6B_", "B17_7B_",
  "D30B_", "D31B_"
)

missing_check <- lapply(63:72, function(y) {

  column_names <- paste0(check_vars, y)
  components <- raw_data[, column_names, drop = FALSE]

  stopifnot(all(vapply(components, is.numeric, logical(1))))

  # Number of nonmissing components in each household-year
  n_observed <- rowSums(!is.na(components))

  # Reproduce the original calculation ONLY to diagnose missingness
  original_sum <- rowSums(components, na.rm = TRUE)

  data.frame(
    year = 2000 + y,
    total = nrow(components),
    all_missing = sum(n_observed == 0),
    partially_missing = sum(
      n_observed > 0 & n_observed < length(check_vars)
    ),
    complete = sum(n_observed == length(check_vars)),
    all_missing_but_sum_zero = sum(
      n_observed == 0 & original_sum == 0
    )
  )
})

missing_check <- bind_rows(missing_check)

kable(
  missing_check,
  caption = "Missingness in the original GFP components"
)
```

## 6. Running Models
### A. Plots
GFP is measured in rupees, using the crop-price conversions in Section 3.
The analysis covers Nepali years 2064–2071.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

analysis_data <- remit_l |>
  filter(year >= 64, year <= 71) |>
  mutate(
    year_bs = 2000 + year,
    time = year - 64,
    hhid = factor(hhid),
    ethnic = factor(ethnic),
    log_rem = log1p(rem),
    log_labor = log1p(hired_lab),
    log_land = log1p(land_avg)
  )

component_names <- c(
  "B11C_", "B12C_", "B13C_", "B14C_", "B15C_",
  "B16B_",
  "B17_1B_", "B17_2B_", "B17_3B_", "B17_4B_",
  "B17_5B_", "B17_6B_", "B17_7B_",
  "D30B_", "D31B_"
)

model_raw <- temp_env[[loaded_names[1]]]

component_counts <- data.frame()

for (y in 64:71) {

  components <- model_raw[
    , paste0(component_names, y)
  ]

  year_counts <- data.frame(
    hhid = model_raw$HHID,
    year = y,
    n_components = rowSums(!is.na(components))
  )

  component_counts <- rbind(
    component_counts,
    year_counts
  )
}

analysis_data <- analysis_data |>
  left_join(component_counts, by = c("hhid", "year")) |>
  mutate(
    gfp_preview = ifelse(
      n_components == 0,
      NA,
      gfp
    ),
    log_gfp = log1p(gfp_preview)
  )

```

### B. Run model
#### i. Mutli-level for continuous outcome
```{r}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

# Prepare a common analysis sample
# Keep the same households and observations
# for all model comparisons

model_data <- analysis_data |>
  filter(
    is.finite(log_gfp),
    is.finite(log_rem),
    is.finite(log_labor),
    is.finite(farm_tech),
    is.finite(log_land),
    !is.na(time),
    !is.na(ethnic),
    !is.na(hhid)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    hhid = factor(hhid),
    ethnic = factor(ethnic),
    time_f = factor(time)
  ) |>
  droplevels()

# Check sample size
cat("Observations:", nrow(model_data), "\n")
cat("Households:", n_distinct(model_data$hhid), "\n")
table(model_data$time_f)
```

####Empty Model (Unconditional Model)

```{r}
# Random intercept only
m0 <- lmer(
  log_gfp ~ 1 + (1 | hhid),
  data = model_data,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(m0)

# Calculate ICC
vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m0))

var_hh <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "hhid"]
var_resid <- sigma(m0)^2

ICC <- var_hh / (var_hh + var_resid)

cat("Household variance:", var_hh, "\n")
cat("Residual variance:", var_resid, "\n")
cat("ICC:", ICC, "\n")
```

####Add Level-1 Fixed Effects

```{r}
# Time, remittances, labor, farm technology and land
m1 <- lmer(
  log_gfp ~ time_f + log_rem +
    log_labor + farm_tech + log_land +
    (1 | hhid),
  data = model_data,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(m1)
```

####Compare M0 and M1

```{r}
# Refit with ML because fixed effects differ
m0_ml <- update(m0, REML = FALSE)
m1_ml <- update(m1, REML = FALSE)

anova(m0_ml, m1_ml)

# Check AIC and BIC using ML fits
AIC(m0_ml, m1_ml)
BIC(m0_ml, m1_ml)
```

```{r}
# Step 2: Random intercept + random slope for remittances
m2 <- lmer(
  log_gfp ~ time_f + log_rem +
    log_labor + farm_tech + log_land +
    (1 + log_rem | hhid),
  data = model_data,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(m2)
```

```{r}
anova(m1, m2, refit = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# M3: Random Intercept + Remittance and Labor Random Slopes

m3 <- lmer(
  log_gfp ~ time_f + log_rem +
    log_labor + farm_tech + log_land +
    (1 + log_rem + log_labor | hhid),
  data = model_data,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(m3)
```

```{r}
anova(m2, m3, refit = FALSE)
```
```{r}
# M4: Random Intercept + Three Random Slopes
m4 <- lmer(
  log_gfp ~ time_f + log_rem +
    log_labor + farm_tech + log_land +
    (1 + log_rem + log_labor + farm_tech | hhid),
  data = model_data,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(m4)
```
